title: Al-'Alim, the All-Knowing
hookLine: the All-Knowing, who knows what the heart hides

lines: ONE THING NEVER SAID OUT LOUD.
AN OLD MAN, GRAY AND WEAK.
cards: Some things people carry and never say out loud. A fear. A hope that feels too big or too silly.
Something they did. Something done to them. It sits in a back room of the heart, and it's easy to get very good at walking past the door.
Surah Maryam begins with an old man going through that door. Zakariyya, a prophet, his bones weak, his hair gone white, his wife unable to have children.
He calls on his Lord, the surah says, with a cry in secret, a hidden call. Today: Al-'Alim, the All-Knowing.

teach.b: What Zakariyya says is simple and raw: my bones have grown weak, my head is shining with gray, and I have never been disappointed in calling on You. I want someone to carry on after me. Then he waits.
Al-'Alim comes from the root '-l-m, to know. It gives 'ilm, knowledge; 'ulama', scholars; mu'allim, a teacher. The name often closes a verse like a signature: and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
What does He know? Everything, the Qur'an says, but it keeps pointing at the small and the hidden. In al-An'am, not a leaf falls but He knows it.
In Ta Ha, if you speak aloud, He knows the secret and what is even more hidden. In al-Mulk: He knows what is in the breasts; should He not know, the one who created?

And in Surah Qaf, in Pickthall's words: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. So why did Zakariyya say it at all, if Allah already knew?
Muslim teachers often put it this way: du'a isn't news delivered to Allah.
It's the servant turning toward the one who already knows, and being changed by the turning.

Zakariyya's hidden call was answered with glad news: a son, Yahya, John, a name the surah says was given to no one before him. In the surah's telling, the secret call from the back room had a listener the whole time.

how: Muslims make du'a, personal prayer, in any language and at any time, often quietly, following the example of prophets like Zakariyya; some save the night, or the prostration of the prayer, for what they have told no one.

o: the wise one who teaches all the scholars
the one who learns what people tell him in prayer
the one who knows everything, even the hidden

games.q: what's inside the name — tap the pairs.

s: du'a is telling Allah something He doesn't know
Muslims say it's turning toward the one who already knows.
al-'Alim often closes a verse, like a signature
e.g. and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
the Qur'an says a falling leaf is too small for Allah to know
al-An'am: not a leaf falls but He knows it.

games.q: you're Zakariyya: old, gray, childless. alone at night, what do you do?
o: accept it silently and never ask
call on your Lord with a hidden call and say it plainly
announce your wish in the temple
games.why: he called in secret, saying his bones were weak and his hair gray. he was answered with glad news of a son, Yahya (19:2–7).

practice: Somewhere you won't be interrupted, let your breath slow and let the back-room thing come forward, the one you haven't said to anyone, without fixing or explaining it.

If you pray, tell Allah silently, in plain words, the way Zakariyya did; if you don't, say it to yourself honestly in the quiet, and let it be known by you. Then rest in what it's like for the thing to be said and not hidden.

wordCard.voice: Al-'Alim. The All-Knowing, who knows the leaf that falls, the secret and what's more hidden still: what the heart hides. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the All-Knowing, from '-l-m, to know.

carryVoice: Your line: he already knows. No performance needed for the one who knows the back room. That's two hundred forty-seven days.

sources.q: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.

sources.ref: Qur'an 19:2–7 (Zakariyya's hidden call and the news of Yahya)
Qur'an 6:59; 20:7; 67:13–14 (the falling leaf; the secret and more hidden; He knows what is in the breasts)
